answerNotes.BOOT: A boot rises above the ankle. Its sole can leave a tread pattern in mud or snow.
answerNotes.PRINT: A print can be an image or an impression. In snow, it is the mark left by a foot or shoe rather than words on paper.
answerNotes.SNOW: Snow falls as ice crystals or groups of crystals. It differs from liquid rain and the hard pellets of hail.
answerNotes.SOLE: The sole is the shoe's bottom. The tread is the pattern on its outer surface that contacts the ground.
answerNotes.PATH: A path is a route for walking. Stepping stones can mark that route without making a continuous paved surface.
answerNotes.STEP: Step can name an action or one level of a stairway. In a stepping-stone clue, it concerns placing a foot on the next surface.
answerNotes.WHITE: White is a color description, not a flower or bird name. Crossings can help when a clue asks for a color rather than a species.
answerNotes.FOOT: A foot is a body part and also a unit of length. A shoe clue points to the body meaning rather than twelve inches.
answerNotes.WINTER: Winter is the cold season in much of the United States. Snow scenes are familiar examples rather than conditions experienced everywhere.
